principles: Dirty classification must be centralized and typed, not scattered as string-prefix checks in lifecycle handlers.
This story may improve visibility but must not loosen TEST/DONE blocking behavior.
Existing runtime artifact and story metadata registries should remain the source of path semantics where they already exist.
drivers: B-c9f5 showed raw dirty gate output can cause REVIEW/TEST loops and poor operator diagnosis.
Lifecycle gates and session brief need the same classification vocabulary.
The next generated-artifact story needs a stable extension point.

options.name: A: Add a core dirty-worktree classifier consumed by gate rendering
pros: Creates a single typed surface for lifecycle gates and future artifact declarations.
Keeps story-advance smaller by moving path ownership logic out of handler code.
Can be covered with focused unit/smoke assertions without changing policy first.
cons: Requires touching gate presentation and tests now, before the allowlist story can consume the declared-artifact category.

options.name: B: Patch story_advance dirty hint with local path groups
pros: Smallest immediate diff and directly improves current DONE hint text.
cons: Keeps path semantics inside story_advance, duplicating evidence-freshness and runtime registry logic.
Would make later generated artifact support another local patch instead of a registry consumer.

options.name: C: Skip classifier and auto-commit Koala metadata first
pros: Could reduce one field loop quickly when validate writes only Koala metadata.
cons: Does not distinguish generated product artifacts from unexpected material dirty files.
Risks changing blocking behavior before the system can explain dirty ownership categories.

chosen: A: Add a core dirty-worktree classifier consumed by gate rendering
rationale: Choose A because the reported failure is a classification and gate vocabulary problem, not only a metadata cleanup problem. A keeps current blocking conservative while creating the typed entry point required by later metadata auto-commit and generated artifact declaration stories.

preMortem.scenario: Classifier accidentally labels source or fixture changes as safe metadata.
preMortem.trigger: A broad prefix or runtime-artifact matcher overlaps packages/main/src, packages/main/tests, or koala.config paths.
preMortem.consequence: DONE gate could under-report material changes and reduce review quality.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep this story policy-conservative and add smoke assertions that source/config/fixture paths classify as material or unexpected, not koala metadata.

preMortem.scenario: Gate output improves classification but loses the original dirty path details users need.
preMortem.trigger: Rendering summarizes categories without listing representative status rows.
preMortem.consequence: Users still cannot fix the dirty state quickly.
preMortem.mitigation: Render category counts plus sample status rows, keeping the raw status code and path in the hint.

preMortem.scenario: The new helper duplicates existing metadata/runtime registries and drifts later.
preMortem.trigger: Implementing standalone string prefixes instead of importing evidence-freshness and runtime-artifact-registry helpers.
preMortem.consequence: One gate can classify a path differently from freshness/material hash logic.
preMortem.mitigation: Consume existing registry helpers and add focused tests around story metadata, runtime artifacts, material source, fixture, config, and product output examples.
